report:
The displayed restricted warped-path theorem checks out mathematically. I found no concrete defect in its volume formula, minimizing metrics, endpoint passage, cost profiles, nonbigness proof, or stated modification comparisons. Exact task completion remains uncertified: novelty relative to the mentioned companion manuscripts cannot be checked from the supplied overlap notes, and the submitted article omits the requested Morse-bound comparison. The unspecified historical residual-jump claims are also not independently established here. These limitations do not invalidate the restricted endpoint theorem or justify declaring the original programme closed.

The smooth existence application is valid. On the closed Kähler representative Kε, the target density is smooth, strictly positive, and has mass Wε. [Tosatti–Weinkove, Corollary 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2) supplies the solution up to a scalar; closed Stokes forces that scalar to be zero. Multiplying its potential by 2π gives the specified dd^c normalization. No uniform endpoint estimate is needed. Independently expanding Ωε^n gives cε μ. Matrix AM–GM and Gauduchon Stokes provide the lower bound for every test. The displayed cofactor γ ε^m is closed: its first term has top base degree, and its second has closed factors. Its numerator nWε and denominator cε^(m/n)Hε attain equality, proving the full-test formula and actual minimizing-test existence.

The cost computation and differentiation agree, including every factor of n and H. Holding any attaining test fixed and using both signs of the path increment proves that every minimizer has the same cost. The short negative-s extension handles s=0. Consequently arbitrary minimizing selections produce the same smooth scalar integrand; no measurable or differentiable metric selection is required. Monotonicity and the fixed-test upper bound establish the actual endpoint infimum, also for Hermitian regularization. Monotone convergence identifies H(0), including infinity. The fundamental theorem on compact segments then proves the finite improper integral without assuming its desired bound.

The tubular estimates reconstruct correctly. Splitting at ε^(1/k) gives H thresholds d/k=1 and J thresholds d/k=2, yielding all five stated integrable profiles. The r>2 limit follows by dominated convergence. Finite disjoint components are controlled by the smallest ratio. The polynomial Wε has nonnegative coefficients and leading order ε^(m−ν), so the volume power order is q+z. Density-comparison and metric-sandwich arguments preserve this order; their constants depend on density bounds and geometry, and give no density-independent exact value.

The modification arguments also work under their stated hypotheses. Vanishing mass of positive nef approximants forces their weak limit to zero; nondegeneracy of the de Rham pairing then gives [χ]^j=0. Pullback preserves ν. Pairing effective divisor currents with positive nef approximants proves ν(χD)≤ν(π*χ). Degree-one integration and σY≥cπ*σB prove zY≥zB. The real-divisor potential must be the weighted sum of individual logarithmic norms, as the final source application correctly specifies. Its normalization agrees with [Demailly V.13.2](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

The nonbigness test is valid for every genuine quasi-psh potential: pullback base top-degree tests are smooth, positive and dd^c-closed, and distributional Stokes eliminates dd^c u. It forces a≥δ everywhere. Conversely, a>0 makes the endpoint itself positive. The projective radial density, H(0)=m/(m−1), endpoint volume (m+1)(m−1)/m, and logarithmic versus finite cost limits are correct. Since X is Kähler, [Demailly–Păun’s positive-mass nef criterion](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0105176) also confirms that these nonbig endpoints cannot contain a closed nef positive-volume core plus a semipositive summand.

For the missing comparison, the Morse inequality concerns usual cohomological volume and d-closed nef real (1,1) classes on a compact Kähler manifold; its general quantitative statement appears in [Tosatti, Theorem 1.1, September 2026](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.30153v2). In the closed subcase a≡a0, take A=α+(a0+t)w and B=tw: its right-hand side is nWa0, exactly the computed endpoint root-volume power Vμ. For nonconstant a, dθ=da∧w and the inverse moment H retains μ-dependence, so the cohomological comparison cannot be transferred to this nonclosed background.

Presentation corrections: define the otherwise undefined symbols a− and a+; the proved logarithmic volume exponent is q+z. Specify that modification ‘equality’ means equality of power orders. It does not include logarithmic comparability or preservation of positive endpoint volume: the quadratic point-blowup case has order zero on both bases but introduces inverse-logarithmic decay.

passages.statement: On a connected compact Hermitian manifold (M,ω) of complex dimension d≥2, every smooth real function F admits a unique real number b and a unique smooth real function ψ normalized by sup_M ψ=0 such that ω+i∂bar∂ψ>0 and (ω+i∂bar∂ψ)^d=e^(F+b)ω^d (Tosatti–Weinkove, arXiv:0910.1390v2, Corollary 1).
passages.quote: there exists a unique real number b and a unique smooth real-valued function ϕ on M solving

passages.statement: For a holomorphic line bundle L on a complex manifold, equipped with a smooth Hermitian metric of Chern curvature Θ(L), and a holomorphic section s not identically zero on any connected component, log||s||² is locally integrable and satisfies (i/(2π))∂bar∂log||s||²=[div(s)]−iΘ(L)/(2π); the effective divisor integration current [div(s)] is positive and closed.
For every compact oriented smooth real N-manifold without boundary, the de Rham cohomology groups are finite dimensional and the integration pairing H^p_dR(M,R)×H^(N−p)_dR(M,R)→R is nondegenerate.

If (M,ω) is a compact Kähler n-fold and τ is a smooth d-closed real (1,1)-form whose class is nef and satisfies ∫_M τ^n>0, then there exist δ>0 and a genuine global quasi-psh function u such that τ+(i/(2π))∂bar∂u≥δω (Demailly–Păun, Theorem 2.12).
passages.quote: contains a Kähler current T, that is, a closed positive current T such that T ≥ δω for some δ > 0.

passages.statement: For a compact Kähler n-fold M and nef real (1,1) cohomology classes A and B, the usual cohomological volume, set to zero outside the pseudoeffective cone, satisfies vol(A−B)≥∫_M A^n−n∫_M A^(n−1)B (Tosatti, arXiv:2608.30153v2, Theorem 1.1).
